'''Mun Mi-ock''' ({{Korean|hangul=문미옥|hanja=文美玉}};<ref>{{Cite web |last=경제인문사회연구회 |first=NRC |title=과학기술정책연구원 문미옥 원장 선임 |url=https://www.nrc.re.kr/board.es?mid=a10108020000&bid=0015&tag=&act=view&list_no=172588&act=view&list_no=172588 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=NRC 경제인문사회연구회 - NRC 공식 홈페이지, NRC |language=ko}}</ref> born 20 December 1968) is a former South Korean research professor at [[Yonsei University]] and [[Ewha Womans University]] serving as the President of Science and Technology Policy Institute from January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-17|title=STEPI 신임 원장에 문미옥 前 과기부 차관|url=https://www.hellodd.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=91406|access-date=2021-08-10|website=헬로디디|language=ko}}</ref> Mun previously served as President [[Moon Jae-in]]'s first [[Office of the President (South Korea)|Science and Technology Advisor]] and his second [[Ministry of Science and ICT|Vice Minister of Science and ICT]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=|script-title=ko:[프로필] 문미옥 과기정통부 제1차관|url=http://m.newspim.com/news/view/20181214000263|access-date=2020-07-06|website=[[NewsPim]]|language=ko}}</ref> - the first woman to assume both posts respectively.

Before entering politics and after leaving academia, Mun had led Planning and Policy Division of Center for Women in Science, Engineering, and Technology (WISET) from 2011 and Science Engineering Technology Cooperative (SETCOOP) from 2013 - both policy instruments of the Ministry to support Korean scientists and innovations.<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=ko:문미옥 과기정통부 1차관…물리학 박사 출신 과학인|url=https://www.mk.co.kr/news/it/view/2018/12/780539/|access-date=2020-07-06|website=[[Maeil Business Newspaper]]|language=ko}}</ref>

Mun was the last person recruited by then-party leader Moon Jae-in for the 2016 general election.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-01-27|script-title=ko:문미옥, 사퇴 밝힌 문재인의 마지막 영입인사..'여성 과학기술인'|url=http://www.newsfreezone.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=6318|access-date=2020-07-06|website=뉴스프리존|language=ko}}</ref> Mun received the number 7 on her party's proportional representation list.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-03-23|script-title=ko:더민주 비례7번에 문미옥 한국여성과학기술센터 기획실장(속보)|url=https://www.edaily.co.kr/news/read?newsId=02866726612586272&mediaCodeNo=257|access-date=2020-07-06|website=[[Edaily]]|language=ko}}</ref>

In 2017 Mun was appointed to the newly created post, an advisor to the president for science and technology, automatically losing her seat at the parliament which was taken by Lee Soo Hyuck, now-[[Embassy of South Korea, Washington, D.C.|South Korean ambassador to the United States]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-06-22|script-title=ko:이수혁 전 독일대사, 민주당 비례대표직 승계|url=https://news.joins.com/article/21691132|access-date=2020-07-06|website=[[JoongAng Ilbo]]|language=ko}}</ref> In 2018 she was reshuffled to Moon's second vice minister of science and ICT.

After leaving the Ministry in 2019, Mun then applied to become her party's candidate for [[Songpa District|Songpa]] A constituency for upcoming 2020 general election but lost.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-03-12|script-title=ko:민주당, '송파갑'.... 조재희 예비후보 공천 최종 확정!'|url=http://www.newsfreezone.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=221097|access-date=2020-07-06|website=뉴스프리존|language=ko}}</ref> In January 2021 Mun was brought back to lead one of government-funded research institutes, the Science and Technology Policy Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About STEPI > History|url=https://www.stepi.re.kr/site/stepien/03/10302000000002020111114.jsp|access-date=2021-08-10|website=www.stepi.re.kr}}</ref>

Mun holds three degrees in physics from a bachelor to a doctorate from [[POSTECH]]. She also completed [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research programmes]] in physics at [[Ewha Womans University]] and [[Yonsei University]] both at which she later worked as research professor.<ref name=":0" />
